compiled_state.description:
## Discovered from

Step-7 parity sweep during rebar-debug on bug `itchy-arbored-peccary` (3907-0110-7688-43bd).

## The rule, stated without naming the site

*Every read that hits a snapshot-store entry must record the hit as recency, by bumping the
entry's `mtime`.* This is the janitor's only victim-selection signal.

ADR 0005 D4 states it: "The janitor evicts LRU by `mtime`, **which the cache bumps explicitly
on every hit**. `atime` is unreliable ..., so it is never used as the recency signal."
`cache.touch_entry` (`src/rebar/_snapshot/cache.py:77-85`) is the mechanism.

## Channel census

| surface | rule holds? |
|---|---|
| code entries via `cache.acquire` | ✔ `cache.py:186`, `:192`, `:196` — `touch_entry(dest)` on all three cache-hit re-checks |
| ticket entries via `materialize_tickets` | **MISSING** — `repo_snapshot.py:676-679`, the `if dest.is_dir(): return str(dest)` cache-hit branch returns without touching |
| eviction (`_evict`) | ✔ n/a — consumes `mtime`, does not produce it |
| `startup_sweep` | ✔ n/a — reconciles bytes, not recency |
| CLI / MCP | ✔ n/a — both reach the store only through the two paths above |

## Consequence

A `tickets-<sha>` entry's `mtime` is frozen at its creation time no matter how many gate runs
read it. To the janitor an actively-used ticket store looks maximally cold, so it sorts FIRST
in the LRU order and is the preferred eviction victim — and these are the largest entries in
the store (~861 MiB each measured in the wild). Eviction itself stays safe (POSIX
delete-on-last-close protects in-flight readers), so this is wasted re-materialization, not
corruption.

## Why it was not fixed in 3907

3907 adds the `max_bytes` store-size cap, which makes size-driven eviction possible for the
first time — so it is what makes this gap consequential. But the cap ships **default-off**, so
3907 introduces no live exposure, and recency is a different rule from 3907's two acceptance
criteria (byte accounting and the cap trigger). Filed rather than absorbed.

Note the adjacency to `smart-disloyal-naga` (8386-a512-4815-4e6b), which covers reuse and
per-review release of these same entries — an un-recorded hit is arguably a reuse that was not
recorded. Whoever picks this up should check for overlap first.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `materialize_tickets` bumps the entry's `mtime` on a cache hit, matching `cache.acquire`.
- [ ] A test observes the frozen `mtime` RED (repeated `materialize_tickets` hits leave `mtime`
      unchanged) and GREEN after.
- [ ] A test pins the consequence: a repeatedly-read `tickets-` entry is NOT the first LRU
      victim ahead of a genuinely older, unread entry.
compiled_state.title: materialize_tickets does not bump mtime on a cache hit, so hot ticket entries look LRU-cold
